title: 先把把手往上提  (Lift the Handle)

segments.t: Qing arrives early for her very first morning at the Courtyard Inn in Chengdu. Behind the front desk, veteran handyman Chen is already pouring strong hot tea. Listen to the conversation in Mandarin first without worrying about catching every word.
早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
纸本子？真的吗？
下雨的时候，纸不会弄丢房间名单。
有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
Now let's walk through the conversation, one line at a time.
早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
'Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?' Before asking about the door, Qing opens with
请问
which literally says 'please ask' and serves as a polite 'excuse me'.
早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
'Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.' Chen sequences two steps cleanly:
先
marks what you do first, and a second small word later introduces 'then push'.
啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
'Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.' When introducing her role, Qing says
前台
literally 'front platform', the everyday Chinese word for a hotel front desk or its clerk.
我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
'I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.' Notice how Chen puts 'early' right before 'arrive', saying 'early arrived ten minutes' rather than tucking 'early' at the end like English.
第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
'On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?' Mandarin leaves question words right where the answer sits, so
在哪里
stays after 'the computer' as 'is at where'.
在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
'In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.' To say 'in the drawer', Mandarin wraps the noun with
抽屉里
putting the word for 'inside' after 'drawer' instead of before it.
下雨的时候，纸不会弄丢房间名单。
'When it rains, paper will not lose the room list.' Chinese turns weather into a two-part action:
下雨
pairs 'fall' with 'rain', literally 'down-rain'.
对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
'Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.' Things with handles you grip take the counting word
把
which is why Chen counts 'eight handle-keys' alongside 'eight rooms'.
第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。

'Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.' Chen echoes his favourite two-step pattern from line two: hot tea comes first, and answering the door waits until second. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.
早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
纸本子？真的吗？
下雨的时候，纸不会弄丢房间名单。
有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
Qing is inside, the eight brass keys are on the board, and her first morning has begun. Don't worry if a few words went past quickly; they come back all week. See you next time.
再见！
